evidenceRequests: Q1: Line 3 device history records and rework-area adhesive/component issue logs, reconciled against lot output, Feb-Oct 2026
Q2: Complained-unit lots cross-referenced with the badge IDs and certifications of technicians who built each lot
Q3: Messages and approvals showing who requested or authorized technician lending to Line 3
output.summary: The zero-deviation result is best explained by suppressed reporting, not real improvement. The supervisor bonus penalty began February 2026, and reports stopped while independent lot rejections and customer complaints rose, with Line 3 lots dominant. Line 3's output gain tracks borrowed technicians (flat output per technician-hour), and most borrowed technicians lack bonding certification. Anonymous and corroborating reports describe off-record rework; the closed hotline case was never reviewed. The tubing switch does not explain the complaints. Restoring reporting (suspend penalty, non-retaliation, amnesty) is preferred and robust. An independent investigation including shipped-lot risk is preferred. Adopting Line 3 as a model and reporter-identification are harmful. Discipline is premature until the investigation confirms falsification. Unknown: the Plant Manager's direct role.
